content:
Apple has filed for a temporary restraining order against OpenAI in its ongoing trade secrets lawsuit. Apple says it will suffer "irreparable harm" from the theft of its trade secrets without a TRO.

In its filing, Apple said it wrote to OpenAI after filing its first lawsuit last month, indicating it was prepared to "seek TRO relief." However, Apple says OpenAI could avoid the filing if it agreed to five demands:

  • Stop accessing or using Apple's confidential information
  • Stop any ongoing use or disclosure
  • Preserve all evidence
  • Allow forensic inspection of devices, cloud storage, emails, Slack, Teams and other databases
  • Search OpenAI's systems for any of Apple's confidential information

According to Apple, OpenAI agreed to the first three demands, but the two parties couldn't agree on the final two.

Apple is therefore asking the court to grant a temporary restraining order, asking a judge to immediately forbid OpenAI from using or obtaining any Apple trade secrets, preserve all evidence, allow Apple to conduct forensic inspections of OpenAI's devices and accounts, and recover any Apple confidential information still in OpenAI's hands.

Apple says:

Apple has also filed a separate motion asking the court to speed up discovery, including early access to documents and out-of-court depositions of OpenAI's key employees and management.

Alongside Apple's filing, OpenAI published its most thorough public response to the lawsuit yet. In a blog post published late at night, OpenAI said the "shoddy, aggressive, and unusually personal" lawsuit did not match Apple's reputation as "one of the greatest companies in history."

A hearing on the restraining order is set for October 1, 2026. The full filing is available below.
